note.title: Window containment: inclusive end is intentional
note.summary: contains(start, end, sample) in sensors/window.py is start <= sample <= end. PR 7 records that the inclusive end is deliberate so a shared boundary sample shows in both adjacent dashboard windows.
note.body:
Behavior at baseline 35089cd: sensors/window.py defines contains(start, end, sample) as start <= sample <= end. Both ends are inclusive. The README says this function decides which dashboard panels show a reading.

Rationale from history: PR 7 (merged, 'Adjust dashboard window comparison') changed the end from exclusive (<) to inclusive (<=). Its description says operators compare neighboring sensor windows, and a sample exactly at the shared end must appear in both panels. It calls the overlap intentional. A maintainer comment in the PR says the inclusive end was kept for that reason. So a sample on the shared boundary appearing in two adjacent windows is expected behavior, not a double-counting bug. A review that proposes restoring a half-open interval would contradict this recorded decision unless the dashboard requirement has changed.

Tests: sensors/test_window.py has one test, test_common_positions. It checks that contains(10, 20, 10) and contains(10, 20, 15) are true and contains(10, 20, 21) is false. It does not test the end boundary (sample == end), so the intentional inclusive-end behavior is not covered by a test. Run with python3 -B sensors/test_window.py, per the README.

Limitations: no registered documentation sources. PR 7 content is a cached default-diff artifact. Its commit linkage, freshness and final merged diff are not verified, and a merge does not prove the decision still applies. No handling of start > end, non-numeric or timestamp inputs was inspected or is documented.

claims.text: contains(start, end, sample) returns start <= sample <= end, so both start and end are inclusive at baseline 35089cd.
The README states that contains decides which dashboard panels show a reading.

PR 7 changed the end comparison from exclusive to inclusive so a sample at the shared end of neighboring windows appears in both panels; the PR description calls this overlap intentional and a maintainer comment confirms it.
The existing test covers sample == start, a mid-window sample and sample past the end (21), but not sample == end, so the inclusive-end decision has no test.

Reviewers should treat overlap at a shared boundary as expected and not as a defect, unless the dashboard requirement has changed. This is inferred from a historical decision whose current applicability is unverified.
